reason: Windows Photos can't open most of what I actually work with (TGA, DDS, EXR, HDR, GLB, OBJ, FBX), so a viewer that does is a real upgrade, not a nice-to-have. I'd still run it from the portable zip first and only make it default once it hasn't misbehaved.
why_switch_or_not: 26 of 32 test formats, with TGA/DDS/EXR/HDR plus GLB/OBJ/FBX in one viewer, is exactly what I hunt for, and the Space-bar preview from Explorer would save me opening Blender or Photoshop just to peek at a texture. I'd switch for the formats and the speed on big folders of textures; I wouldn't switch for the editor or the coffee link. What I can't tell from this page is whether DDS shows mips/alpha/cubemaps properly or whether EXR/HDR tone-mapping is sane, so I'd test those with my own files on day one.
current_app_pros: It's already on every Windows install, nothing to maintain, and it's fine for ordinary PNG/JPG. Zero setup after a Windows reinstall.
current_app_pains: It opens none of my work formats: no TGA, DDS, EXR, HDR or any 3D model, so I double-click and get 'can't open' or a prompt to search the Store. It's also slow to start and to flip through a folder of hundreds of textures.
objection: It's an unknown .exe from one developer at version 0.4.1. The page doesn't say it's code-signed or open source, and I'd be making it the default handler for files I open all day. I'd want to know it's safe before the installer touches my machine.
would_change_my_mind: A public source repo or a signed installer with a clean scan would remove my main doubt. Failing that, if it chokes on my real DDS/EXR files in the first hour, I'd drop it.
